records.literal_gloss: [The] sound of a cry from Horonaim: devastation and great destruction!

en.L: The sound of a cry from Horonaim: \q devastation and great destruction!
en.B: Listen! A cry from Horonaim: \q ruin and great destruction!
en.R: Listen to the cries from Horonaim! \q There is ruin and terrible destruction.

es.L: Voz de clamor desde Horonaim: \q ¡devastación y gran destrucción!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Un grito desde Horonaim: \q ¡ruina y gran destrucción!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} los gritos desde Horonaim! \q Hay ruina y una destrucción terrible.

fr.L: Le bruit d’un cri, de Horonaïm : \q dévastation et grande destruction !
fr.B: Écoutez ! Un cri, de Horonaïm : \q ruine et grande destruction !
fr.R: Écoutez les cris qui viennent de Horonaïm ! \q Il y a des ruines et une terrible destruction.

sw.L: Sauti ya kilio kutoka Horonaimu: \q uharibifu na maangamizi makuu!
sw.B: Sikiliza! Kilio kutoka Horonaimu: \q uharibifu na maangamizi makuu!
sw.R: Sikilizeni vilio kutoka Horonaimu! \q Kuna uharibifu na maangamizi makubwa.

vi.L: Có tiếng kêu la từ Hô-rô-na-im: \q tàn phá và hủy diệt lớn!
vi.B: Hãy nghe! Có tiếng kêu la từ Hô-rô-na-im: \q điêu tàn và hủy diệt lớn!
vi.R: Hãy nghe tiếng kêu la từ Hô-rô-na-im! \q Thành bị tàn phá và hủy diệt khủng khiếp.

ko.L: 호로나임에서 부르짖는 소리가 난다. \q 파멸과 큰 멸망이다!
ko.B: 들어라! 호로나임에서 부르짖는 소리가 들린다. \q 파멸과 큰 멸망이다!
ko.R: 호로나임에서 들려오는 울부짖음을 들어 보아라! \q 파멸과 무서운 멸망이 닥쳤다.

decisions.choice: the sound of a cry: listen, a cry
decisions.reason: "The sound of" at the head of a line often works as a call to listen (Isaiah 40:3, 6; Jeremiah 3:21).

decisions.choice: Horonaim: a town in the south of Moab
decisions.reason: Horonaim lay on the way down from the plateau toward the south (Isaiah 15:5; verses 5 and 34 below). It is also named in Mesha's inscription; its exact site is unknown.

decisions.choice: devastation and great destruction: a pair Jeremiah uses for total ruin
decisions.reason: The two words are the plunder of war and a crushing break (4:6, 20; 6:1; Isaiah 59:7; 60:18). They may be what the cry says, or describe what has caused it.

source.text: נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה מוֹאָ֑ב הִשְׁמִ֥יעוּ זְּעָקָ֖ה צְעִירֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is broken Moab; they have made heard a cry, its little ones.

en.L: Moab is broken; \q its little ones have made a cry heard.
en.B: Moab is shattered; \q its little ones cry out for all to hear.
en.R: Moab is broken. \q Its children are crying out loud.

es.L: Moab ha sido quebrantada; \q sus pequeños han hecho oír su clamor.
es.B: Moab está destrozada; \q sus pequeños gritan para que todos los oigan.
es.R: Moab está quebrantada. \q Sus niños lloran a gritos.

fr.L: Moab est brisé ; \q ses petits ont fait entendre un cri.
fr.B: Moab est brisé ; \q ses petits crient à se faire entendre.
fr.R: Moab est brisé. \q Ses enfants poussent de grands cris.

sw.L: Moabu imevunjika; \q watoto wake wadogo wamepaza kilio.
sw.B: Moabu imevunjwavunjwa; \q watoto wake wadogo wanalia kwa sauti.
sw.R: Moabu imevunjika. \q Watoto wake wanalia kwa sauti kubwa.

vi.L: Mô-áp bị đập tan; \q trẻ nhỏ của nó cất tiếng kêu la.
vi.B: Mô-áp bị nghiền nát; \q trẻ nhỏ của nó kêu khóc vang dội.
vi.R: Mô-áp bị đập tan. \q Trẻ con của nó khóc lớn tiếng.

ko.L: 모압이 부서졌다. \q 그의 어린것들이 부르짖는 소리를 들리게 했다.
ko.B: 모압이 산산이 부서졌다. \q 그의 어린것들이 부르짖는 소리가 멀리까지 들린다.
ko.R: 모압이 부서졌다. \q 그 아이들이 큰 소리로 울부짖는다.

decisions.choice: its little ones: the reading of the Hebrew text
alternatives: they have made a cry heard as far as Zoar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is read as "its little ones", the children, or the humble and weak. The ancient Greek translation reads "to Zoar", from nearly the same letters, which would give "they have made the cry heard as far as Zoar" (compare verse 34; Isaiah 15:5). The Greek reading is given here from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: Moab is broken: the fall pictured as already done
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the completed form speaks of the certain future. The verb "break" returns through the chapter (verses 17, 25, 38, 39).

source.text: כִּ֚י מַעֲלֵ֣ה הַלּוּחִ֔יתבִּבְכִ֖י יַֽעֲלֶה־בֶּ֑כִי כִּ֚י בְּמוֹרַ֣ד חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם צָרֵ֥י צַֽעֲקַת־שֶׁ֖בֶר שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] ascent of the Luhith, with weeping goes up weeping; for on [the] descent of Horonaim [the] distresses of [the] cry of destruction they have heard.

en.L: For [on] the ascent of Luhith \q with weeping, weeping goes up; \q for on the descent of Horonaim \q they have heard the anguish of the cry of ruin.
en.B: Up the climb to Luhith \q they go weeping, weeping all the way; \q on the way down to Horonaim \q they have heard the anguished cry of disaster.
en.R: People climb the hill to Luhith, \q weeping and weeping as they go. \q On the road down to Horonaim \q they hear the painful cries about the disaster.

es.L: Porque [por] la cuesta de Luhit \q con llanto sube el llanto; \q porque en la bajada de Horonaim \q han oído la angustia del grito de destrucción.
es.B: Por la subida de Luhit \q van llorando, llorando sin parar; \q en la bajada hacia Horonaim \q han oído el grito angustioso de la catástrofe.
es.R: La gente sube la cuesta de Luhit \q llorando y llorando mientras camina. \q En el camino que baja a Horonaim \q se oyen los gritos de dolor por la catástrofe.

fr.L: Car [à] la montée de Louhith \q avec des pleurs, les pleurs montent ; \q car à la descente de Horonaïm \q on a entendu l’angoisse du cri de la ruine.
fr.B: Sur la montée de Louhith, \q on monte en pleurant, en pleurant sans cesse ; \q sur la descente de Horonaïm, \q on a entendu des cris d’angoisse devant le désastre.
fr.R: Les gens gravissent la colline de Louhith \q en pleurant et pleurant encore. \q Sur la route qui descend à Horonaïm, \q on entend des cris de douleur à cause du désastre.

sw.L: Kwa maana [katika] mpando wa Luhithi \q kwa kilio, kilio kinapanda; \q kwa maana katika mteremko wa Horonaimu \q wamesikia dhiki ya kilio cha maangamizi.
sw.B: Kwenye mlima wa kupanda kwenda Luhithi \q wanapanda wakilia, wakilia njia yote; \q kwenye njia ya kushuka kwenda Horonaimu \q wamesikia kilio cha uchungu cha maafa.
sw.R: Watu wanapanda mlima kwenda Luhithi, \q wakilia na kulia wanapokwenda. \q Kwenye njia ya kushuka kwenda Horonaimu \q wanasikia vilio vya uchungu kuhusu maafa.

vi.L: Vì trên dốc lên Lu-hít, \q người ta vừa đi lên vừa khóc mãi; \q vì trên dốc xuống Hô-rô-na-im \q người ta nghe tiếng kêu la đau đớn vì sự tàn phá.
vi.B: Trên đường dốc lên Lu-hít, \q người ta vừa đi vừa khóc, khóc suốt dọc đường; \q trên đường xuống Hô-rô-na-im, \q người ta nghe tiếng kêu la thảm thiết vì tai họa.
vi.R: Người ta leo đồi lên Lu-hít, \q vừa đi vừa khóc mãi không thôi. \q Trên đường xuống Hô-rô-na-im, \q người ta nghe tiếng kêu la đau đớn về tai họa.

ko.L: 루힛 비탈길을 \q 울며 또 울며 올라가고, \q 호로나임 내리막길에서 \q 멸망의 울부짖음의 고통을 그들이 들었다.
ko.B: 루힛으로 오르는 비탈길을 \q 그들이 울고 또 울며 올라간다. \q 호로나임으로 내려가는 길에서 \q 멸망을 슬퍼하는 비통한 부르짖음이 들린다.
ko.R: 사람들이 루힛으로 가는 언덕길을 \q 울고 또 울며 올라간다. \q 호로나임으로 내려가는 길에서 \q 재앙 때문에 고통스럽게 울부짖는 소리가 들린다.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Luhith, the descent of Horonaim: Isaiah 15:5 taken up
decisions.reason: The verse repeats Isaiah 15:5 with changes: Isaiah has "they go up it" where this verse has "weeping goes up" (one letter different), "the road to Horonaim" where this has "the descent of Horonaim", and "they raise a cry of ruin" where this has "they have heard the anguish of the cry of ruin". Both places lay on the route of flight to the south; their sites are unknown.

decisions.choice: with weeping, weeping goes up: weeping on weeping
decisions.reason: The doubled word stresses grief without end. The line may also be read "with weeping one goes up, weeping"; the sense is the same: the refugees weep all the way up the slope.

decisions.choice: the anguish of the cry of ruin: a cry full of distress
alternatives: the enemies have heard the cry of ruin
decisions.reason: The first word most likely means "distresses", so that the cry is an anguished one. The same letters can mean "enemies", giving "the enemies have heard the cry of ruin". The ancient Greek translation has no word for it (a claim from general knowledge), and Isaiah 15:5 has a different verb.

decisions.choice: Luhith: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The written letters here differ slightly from the name's spelling; the reading tradition gives Luhith, as in Isaiah 15:5.

decisions.choice: the climb to / the way down to
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the wording of Isaiah 15:5 ("Up the climb to Luhith") and gives the new word "descent" as "the way down".

source.text: נֻ֖סוּ מַלְּט֣וּ נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וְתִֽהְיֶ֕ינָה כַּעֲרוֹעֵ֖ר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Flee, save your lives, and let them be like a juniper in the wilderness.

en.L: Flee! Save your lives, \q and be like a juniper in the wilderness!
en.B: Run! Save your lives! \q Be like a bare shrub in the wilderness!
en.R: Run away and save your lives! \q Live like a lonely bush in the desert.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Huyan|Huid}}! ¡{{plural_you:Salven|Salvad}} {{plural_you:sus vidas|vuestras vidas}}, \q y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} como un enebro en el desierto!
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Corran|Corred}}! ¡{{plural_you:Salven|Salvad}} {{plural_you:sus vidas|vuestras vidas}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como una mata pelada en el desierto!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Huyan|Huid}} y {{plural_you:salven|salvad}} {{plural_you:sus vidas|vuestras vidas}}! \q {{plural_you:Vivan|Vivid}} como un arbusto solitario en el desierto.

fr.L: Fuyez ! Sauvez vos vies, \q et soyez comme un genévrier dans le désert !
fr.B: Fuyez ! Sauvez votre vie ! \q Soyez comme un arbuste dénudé dans le désert !
fr.R: Fuyez et sauvez votre vie ! \q Vivez comme un buisson isolé dans le désert.

sw.L: Kimbieni! Okoeni nafsi zenu, \q mkawe kama mreteni nyikani!
sw.B: Kimbieni! Okoeni maisha yenu! \q Muwe kama kichaka kikavu nyikani!
sw.R: Kimbieni, mkaokoe maisha yenu! \q Ishini kama kichaka kilicho peke yake jangwani.

vi.L: Hãy chạy trốn! Hãy cứu mạng sống mình, \q và hãy như cây bách xù trong hoang mạc!
vi.B: Hãy chạy đi! Hãy cứu mạng sống mình! \q Hãy như bụi cây trơ trụi trong hoang mạc!
vi.R: Hãy chạy trốn và cứu mạng sống mình! \q Hãy sống như bụi cây lẻ loi trong sa mạc.

ko.L: 도망하여라! 너희 목숨을 구하여라. \q 광야의 노간주나무처럼 되어라!
ko.B: 도망하여라! 목숨을 건져라! \q 광야에 홀로 선 덤불처럼 되어라!
ko.R: 도망하여 목숨을 구하여라! \q 사막에 홀로 서 있는 덤불처럼 살아라.

decisions.choice: like a juniper in the wilderness: a lone shrub in dry land
alternatives: like a wild donkey in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The word names a desert shrub, perhaps a juniper, used in 17:6 for someone stripped and alone. The refugees will live like it, bare and cut off in the wilderness. The same letters spell Aroer, the town of verse 19, so some read "be like Aroer in the wilderness". The ancient Greek translation reads "like a wild donkey", from a word that looks similar (a claim from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: be: the verb is feminine plural
decisions.reason: The commands "flee" and "save" are masculine plural, but "be" is feminine plural. It may agree with "lives" (a feminine word): "let your lives be like a shrub". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a bare shrub
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the wording of 17:6 for the same shrub; Literal keeps "juniper".

decisions.choice: Live like a lonely bush
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means: the refugees will live alone in the desert like a single bush (m1).

decisions.choice: un enebro (L); una mata pelada (B); un arbusto solitario (R)
decisions.reason: The plant (*ʿaroʿer*) is a juniper or a bare desert shrub; the word also sounds like the town Aroer (verse 19).

decisions.choice: "mreteni" (juniper, L); "kichaka kikavu" (B); "kichaka kilicho peke yake" (R)
decisions.reason: The plant is uncertain, a juniper or a bare desert shrub; Literal names the juniper as the English Literal does, and Balanced and Readable describe a lone shrub in dry land.

decisions.choice: "노간주나무" (L); "덤불" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal names the shrub as the English Literal does ("juniper"); the meaning decision says it is a lone shrub in dry land, and Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: כִּ֠י יַ֣עַן בִּטְחֵ֤ךְ בְּמַעֲשַׂ֨יִךְ֙ וּבְא֣וֹצְרוֹתַ֔יִךְ גַּם־אַ֖תְּ תִּלָּכֵ֑דִי וְיָצָ֤א כְמוֹשׁ֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֔ה כֹּהֲנָ֥יו וְשָׂרָ֖יו יַחְדָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: For because you trusted in your works and in your treasures, also you will be captured; and will go out Chemosh into exile, his priests and his princes together.

en.L: For because you trusted in your works and in your treasures, \q you too will be captured; \q and Chemosh will go out into exile, \q his priests and his princes together.
en.B: Because you trusted in your achievements and your treasures, \q you too will be taken. \q Chemosh will go off into exile, \q together with his priests and his officials.
en.R: You trusted in the things you had done and in your riches. \q So you too will be captured. \q Your god Chemosh will be carried away to a foreign land, \q along with his priests and leaders.

es.L: Porque por cuanto confiaste en tus obras y en tus tesoros, \q también tú serás tomada; \q y Quemos saldrá al destierro, \q sus sacerdotes y sus príncipes juntamente.
es.B: Por haber confiado en tus logros y en tus tesoros, \q también tú serás capturada. \q Quemos irá al destierro, \q junto con sus sacerdotes y sus jefes.
es.R: Confiaste en lo que habías hecho y en tus riquezas. \q Por eso también tú serás capturada. \q Tu dios Quemos será llevado a una tierra extranjera, \q junto con sus sacerdotes y sus dirigentes.

fr.L: Car parce que tu t’es confié en tes œuvres et en tes trésors, \q toi aussi tu seras pris ; \q et Kemosh s’en ira en exil, \q ses prêtres et ses princes ensemble.
fr.B: Parce que tu t’es confié en tes réussites et en tes trésors, \q toi aussi tu seras capturé. \q Kemosh partira en exil, \q avec ses prêtres et ses chefs.
fr.R: Tu as mis ta confiance dans ce que tu avais fait et dans tes richesses. \q Alors toi aussi, tu seras capturé. \q Ton dieu Kemosh sera emmené dans un pays étranger, \q avec ses prêtres et ses chefs.

sw.L: Kwa maana kwa sababu uliyatumaini matendo yako na hazina zako, \q wewe nawe utatwaliwa; \q na Kemoshi atakwenda uhamishoni, \q makuhani wake na wakuu wake pamoja.
sw.B: Kwa sababu ulitegemea mafanikio yako na hazina zako, \q wewe nawe utatekwa. \q Kemoshi atachukuliwa uhamishoni, \q pamoja na makuhani wake na maafisa wake.
sw.R: Uliyategemea mambo uliyoyafanya na utajiri wako. \q Kwa hiyo wewe nawe utatekwa. \q Mungu wako Kemoshi atachukuliwa mpaka nchi ya kigeni, \q pamoja na makuhani wake na viongozi wake.

vi.L: Vì ngươi đã tin cậy vào công việc và kho báu của mình, \q nên ngươi cũng sẽ bị bắt; \q và Kê-móc sẽ đi lưu đày, \q cùng với các thầy tế lễ và các quan trưởng của nó.
vi.B: Vì ngươi đã tin cậy vào thành tựu và kho báu của mình, \q nên ngươi cũng sẽ bị bắt. \q Kê-móc sẽ bị đày đi, \q cùng với các thầy tế lễ và các quan chức của nó.
vi.R: Ngươi đã tin cậy vào những việc ngươi làm và vào của cải của ngươi. \q Vì thế ngươi cũng sẽ bị bắt. \q Thần Kê-móc của ngươi sẽ bị đem đi xứ lạ, \q cùng với các thầy tế lễ và các nhà lãnh đạo của nó.

ko.L: 네가 네 업적과 네 보물을 의지했기 때문에, \q 너도 사로잡힐 것이다. \q 그모스가 포로가 되어 끌려가고, \q 그의 제사장들과 그의 고관들도 함께 [끌려갈 것이다].
ko.B: 네가 네가 이룬 것과 네 보물을 의지했으니, \q 너도 사로잡힐 것이다. \q 그모스는 포로가 되어 끌려가고, \q 그의 제사장들과 관리들도 함께 끌려갈 것이다.
ko.R: 너는 네가 이룬 일과 네 재물을 믿었다. \q 그러니 너도 사로잡힐 것이다. \q 너희 신 그모스도 남의 나라로 끌려갈 것이다. \q 그의 제사장들과 지도자들도 함께 끌려갈 것이다.

decisions.choice: your works and your treasures: what Moab had made and stored up
decisions.reason: "Works" can mean deeds or the things a people has made, such as fortresses and cities; with "treasures" it means Moab's achievements and wealth. The ancient Greek translation reads "your strongholds" (a claim from general knowledge). Trusting in such things instead of God is a theme of Jeremiah (9:22; 17:5).

decisions.choice: Chemosh: the god of Moab
decisions.reason: Chemosh was the national god of the Moabites (Numbers 21:29; Judges 11:24). Solomon built him a high place near Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7), which Josiah tore down (2 Kings 23:13). The written text spells the name slightly differently here; the reading tradition gives the usual form.

decisions.choice: Chemosh will go into exile: the god cannot save even himself
decisions.reason: Conquerors carried off the statues of defeated nations' gods with their priests and leaders (Isaiah 46:1-2; Jeremiah 43:12). The god Moab trusted is taken captive with the people. The line is close to Amos 1:15, said of Ammon's king, and Jeremiah 49:3 says it again of Milcom.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this word (sar) in a court setting.

decisions.choice: Your god ... carried away to a foreign land
decisions.reason: Readable says who Chemosh is and what exile means (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: Quemos
decisions.reason: The god of Moab, as published 1 Kings 11:7 and 2 Kings 23:13.

decisions.choice: "Kemosh"
decisions.reason: The published French form of the god of Moab (1 Kings 11:7).

decisions.choice: Kê-móc
decisions.reason: The god of Moab is written as 1 Kings 11:7 and 2 Kings 23:13 have him; Readable adds "thần", as the English adds "your god".

decisions.choice: "그모스"
decisions.reason: The form published in 1 Kings 11:7 and the Kings tables.

source.text: וְיָבֹ֨א שֹׁדֵ֜ד אֶל־כָּל־עִ֗יר וְעִיר֙ לֹ֣א תִמָּלֵ֔ט וְאָבַ֥ד הָעֵ֖מֶק וְנִשְׁמַ֣ד הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will come a destroyer to every city, and a city not will escape; and will perish the valley, and will be destroyed the plateau, as has said Yahweh.

en.L: And a destroyer will come against every town, and no town will escape; \q the valley will perish, and the plateau will be destroyed, \q as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.
en.B: The destroyer will come upon every town; not one town will escape. \q The valley will be ruined and the plateau laid waste, \q just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.
en.R: The enemy who destroys will attack every town. Not one town will escape. \q The valley will be ruined, and the high plain will be destroyed. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this will happen.

es.L: Y vendrá el destructor a toda ciudad, y ninguna ciudad escapará; \q y perecerá el valle, y será destruida la llanura, \q como ha dicho {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: El destructor vendrá contra todas las ciudades; ni una ciudad escapará. \q El valle quedará arruinado y la meseta devastada, \q tal como lo ha dicho {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: El enemigo que destruye atacará todas las ciudades. Ni una sola escapará. \q El valle quedará arruinado, y la llanura alta será destruida. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho que así sucederá.

fr.L: Et le dévastateur viendra contre toute ville, et aucune ville n’échappera ; \q la vallée périra, et le plateau sera détruit, \q comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a dit.
fr.B: Le dévastateur viendra sur chaque ville ; pas une ville n’échappera. \q La vallée sera ruinée et le plateau ravagé, \q comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a dit.
fr.R: L’ennemi destructeur attaquera chaque ville. Pas une seule ville n’échappera. \q La vallée sera ruinée et le haut plateau sera détruit. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit que cela arriverait.

sw.L: Naye mharibu atakuja juu ya kila mji, wala hakuna mji utakaookoka; \q bonde litaangamia, na uwanda utaharibiwa, \q kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema.
sw.B: Mharibu atakuja juu ya kila mji; hakuna mji hata mmoja utakaookoka. \q Bonde litaharibiwa na uwanda wa juu utafanywa ukiwa, \q kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema.
sw.R: Adui mwangamizi atashambulia kila mji. Hakuna mji hata mmoja utakaookoka. \q Bonde litaharibiwa, na nchi tambarare ya juu itaangamizwa. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema kwamba haya yatatokea.

vi.L: Kẻ tàn phá sẽ đến đánh mọi thành, không thành nào thoát khỏi; \q thung lũng sẽ bị hủy hoại, cao nguyên sẽ bị tàn phá, \q như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.B: Kẻ hủy diệt sẽ đến từng thành; không một thành nào thoát khỏi. \q Thung lũng sẽ điêu tàn, cao nguyên sẽ bị tàn phá, \q đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán.
vi.R: Quân hủy diệt sẽ tấn công mọi thành. Không một thành nào thoát khỏi. \q Thung lũng sẽ bị tàn phá, cao nguyên sẽ bị hủy diệt. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán điều ấy sẽ xảy ra.

ko.L: 그리고 멸망시키는 자가 모든 성읍에 올 것이니, 한 성읍도 피하지 못할 것이다. \q 골짜기가 망하고, 평지가 황폐해질 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 대로이다.
ko.B: 파괴자가 모든 성읍에 들이닥칠 것이니, 한 성읍도 벗어나지 못할 것이다. \q 골짜기는 망하고 고원은 황폐해질 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 그대로이다.
ko.R: 파괴하는 원수가 모든 성읍을 공격할 것이다. 한 성읍도 피하지 못할 것이다. \q 골짜기는 망하고, 높은 평원은 황폐해질 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그렇게 되리라고 말씀하셨다.

decisions.choice: the valley and the plateau: the two parts of Moab's land
decisions.reason: "The plateau" is the high tableland north of the Arnon, with towns such as Heshbon, Dibon and Medeba (verse 21; Deuteronomy 3:10; Joshua 13:9). "The valley" is most likely the Jordan valley below it, on the east side of the river (Joshua 13:27).

decisions.choice: a destroyer: the invading army
decisions.reason: The word is the same as in 6:26 and returns in verses 18 and 32. The destroyer is not named; in the setting of chapters 46-51 it is Babylon.

decisions.choice: The enemy who destroys
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the destroyer is an enemy army (m2).

source.text: תְּנוּ־צִ֣יץ לְמוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י נָצֹ֖א תֵּצֵ֑א וְעָרֶ֨יהָ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Give wings to Moab, for flying away she will go out; and her cities a desolation will become, without inhabitant in them.

en.L: Give wings to Moab, \q for she will surely fly away; \q and her towns will become a desolation, \q with no one living in them.
en.B: Give Moab wings, \q for she must fly away; \q her towns will become a wasteland, \q with no one left living there.
en.R: Give Moab wings, \q because it must fly away. \q Its towns will become ruins, \q and no one will live in them.

es.L: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} alas a Moab, \q porque volando saldrá; \q y sus ciudades se convertirán en desolación, \q sin quien habite en ellas.
es.B: {{plural_you:Denle|Dadle}} alas a Moab, \q porque tiene que huir volando; \q sus ciudades quedarán desoladas, \q sin nadie que viva en ellas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Denle|Dadle}} alas a Moab, \q porque tiene que escapar volando. \q Sus ciudades quedarán en ruinas, \q y nadie vivirá en ellas.

fr.L: Donnez des ailes à Moab, \q car elle s’envolera sûrement ; \q et ses villes deviendront une désolation, \q sans personne qui y habite.
fr.B: Donnez des ailes à Moab, \q car elle doit s’envoler ; \q ses villes deviendront un désert, \q sans plus personne pour y habiter.
fr.R: Donnez des ailes à Moab, \q parce qu’il doit s’envoler. \q Ses villes deviendront des ruines, \q et personne n’y habitera.

sw.L: Mpeni Moabu mabawa, \q kwa maana hakika ataruka aende zake; \q nayo miji yake itakuwa ukiwa, \q bila mtu wa kukaa ndani yake.
sw.B: Mpeni Moabu mabawa, \q kwa maana ni lazima aruke aende zake; \q miji yake itakuwa nyika, \q bila mtu anayebaki kuishi humo.
sw.R: Ipeni Moabu mabawa, \q kwa sababu ni lazima iruke iende zake. \q Miji yake itakuwa magofu, \q wala hakuna mtu atakayeishi ndani yake.

vi.L: Hãy cho Mô-áp đôi cánh, \q vì nó chắc chắn sẽ bay đi; \q các thành của nó sẽ thành hoang vu, \q không ai ở trong đó.
vi.B: Hãy cho Mô-áp đôi cánh, \q vì nó phải bay đi; \q các thành của nó sẽ thành chốn hoang vu, \q không còn ai ở.
vi.R: Hãy cho Mô-áp đôi cánh, \q vì nó phải bay đi. \q Các thành của nó sẽ thành đống đổ nát, \q và không ai sống ở đó.

ko.L: 모압에게 날개를 주어라. \q 그가 반드시 날아서 나갈 것이다. \q 그의 성읍들이 황무지가 되어 \q 그 안에 사는 사람이 없을 것이다.
ko.B: 모압에게 날개를 달아 주어라. \q 그가 날아서 도망쳐야 한다. \q 그의 성읍들은 황무지가 되고, \q 거기에 사는 사람이 아무도 없을 것이다.
ko.R: 모압에게 날개를 달아 주어라. \q 모압은 날아서 도망쳐야 한다. \q 모압의 성읍들은 폐허가 될 것이다. \q 거기에 사는 사람이 아무도 없을 것이다.

decisions.choice: wings: the sense of the word is uncertain
alternatives: set up a gravestone for Moab
decisions.reason: The word usually means a flower or a shining plate (Isaiah 40:7; Exodus 28:36). Here, beside the verb "fly", it is most likely "wings" or "a wing": Moab must escape as a bird does. Other suggested senses are "salt", which an enemy spread on a ruined town so that nothing would grow (Judges 9:45), and "a gravestone" or marker. The ancient Greek translation reads "signs" (a claim from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: she will surely fly away: a doubled verb for emphasis
decisions.reason: A rare verb, "fly" (natsa), is joined to the common verb "go out" (yatsa), which sound alike; together they mean a sudden, certain flight. The rare verb also sounds like the noun of the first line.

decisions.choice: a desolation: an empty, frightening ruin
decisions.reason: The word is one of Jeremiah's for a land left waste, a horror to those who see it (2:15; 4:7; 25:11).

decisions.choice: it ... Its towns
decisions.reason: Moab is "she" in the Hebrew, as lands often are. Literal and Balanced keep "she"; Readable says "it".

decisions.choice: "날개"
decisions.reason: The English reads "wings"; the meaning decision says the word is uncertain, and Korean follows the English reading.

source.text: אָר֗וּר עֹשֶׂ֛ה מְלֶ֥אכֶת יְהוָ֖ה רְמִיָּ֑ה וְאָר֕וּר מֹנֵ֥עַ חַרְבּ֖וֹ מִדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Cursed [is one who] does [the] work of Yahweh [with] slackness, and cursed [is one who] holds back his sword from blood.

en.L: Cursed [is] the one who does the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with slackness, \q and cursed [is] the one who holds back his sword from blood.
en.B: Cursed is anyone who does the work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} carelessly, \q and cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from shedding blood.
en.R: A curse on anyone who is lazy in doing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s work! \q A curse on anyone who holds back his sword and does not use it!

es.L: Maldito el que hace la obra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} con flojedad, \q y maldito el que detiene su espada de la sangre.
es.B: Maldito sea quien hace la obra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} con descuido, \q y maldito sea quien impide que su espada derrame sangre.
es.R: ¡Maldito el que es perezoso para hacer la obra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¡Maldito el que retiene su espada y no la usa!

fr.L: Maudit [soit] celui qui fait l’œuvre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} avec négligence, \q et maudit [soit] celui qui retient son épée loin du sang.
fr.B: Maudit soit quiconque fait l’œuvre {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} avec négligence, \q et maudit soit quiconque empêche son épée de verser le sang.
fr.R: Malédiction sur celui qui fait mollement le travail {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Malédiction sur celui qui retient son épée et ne s’en sert pas !

sw.L: Amelaaniwa yeye aifanyaye kazi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa ulegevu, \q na amelaaniwa yeye auzuiaye upanga wake usimwage damu.
sw.B: Amelaaniwa kila mtu aifanyaye kazi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa uzembe, \q na amelaaniwa kila mtu auzuiaye upanga wake usimwage damu.
sw.R: Laana juu ya mtu yeyote aliye mvivu katika kuifanya kazi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Laana juu ya mtu yeyote anayeuzuia upanga wake asiutumie!

vi.L: Đáng rủa thay kẻ làm công việc của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cách biếng nhác, \q và đáng rủa thay kẻ giữ gươm mình không cho vấy máu.
vi.B: Đáng nguyền rủa cho kẻ làm công việc của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cách cẩu thả, \q và đáng nguyền rủa cho kẻ giữ gươm mình không cho đổ máu.
vi.R: Đáng nguyền rủa cho kẻ lười biếng khi làm công việc của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! \q Đáng nguyền rủa cho kẻ giữ gươm lại mà không dùng đến!

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 일을 게을리하는 자는 저주를 받을 것이다. \q 자기 칼을 피에서 거두는 자도 저주를 받을 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 일을 소홀히 하는 자는 저주를 받을 것이다. \q 칼을 거두어 피를 흘리지 않는 자도 저주를 받을 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 일을 게으르게 하는 사람은 저주를 받아라! \q 칼을 거두고 쓰지 않는 사람도 저주를 받아라!

decisions.choice: the work of the LORD: the judgment on Moab, carried out by its attackers
decisions.reason: The invaders are doing God's work when they strike Moab, as Babylon is God's servant in 25:9 and 27:6. A curse on one who holds back recalls Saul, who spared what God had given to destruction (1 Samuel 15:9, 23), and Ahab, who let Ben-hadad go (1 Kings 20:42). The saying does not praise violence in itself; it says the judgment will be carried out in full.

decisions.choice: with slackness: half-heartedly or deceitfully
decisions.reason: The word means both slack, lazy work (Proverbs 10:4; 12:24) and deceit (Psalm 52:4). Here it is work done carelessly, without full effort.

decisions.choice: cursed ... cursed: a double curse formula
decisions.reason: "Cursed is the one who" is the form of the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 27:15-26; Jeremiah 11:3; 17:5). The verse is prose-like in length, but the accents divide it into two parallel halves and it is set in lines with the rest of the poem.

decisions.choice: A curse on anyone ... does not use it
decisions.reason: Readable puts the curse as an exclamation and says "does not use it" for "holds back from blood".

source.text: שַׁאֲנַ֨ן מוֹאָ֜ב מִנְּעוּרָ֗יו וְשֹׁקֵ֥ט הוּא֙ אֶל־שְׁמָרָ֔יו וְלֹֽא־הוּרַ֤ק מִכְּלִי֙ אֶל־כֶּ֔לִי וּבַגּוֹלָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָלָ֑ךְ עַל־כֵּ֗ן עָמַ֤ד טַעְמוֹ֙ בּ֔וֹ וְרֵיח֖וֹ לֹ֥א נָמָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: At ease has been Moab from his youth, and undisturbed he [has been] on his dregs, and not has he been emptied from vessel to vessel, and into exile not has he gone; therefore has remained his taste in him, and his scent not has changed.

en.L: Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs; \q he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, \q and into exile he has not gone; \q therefore his taste has remained in him, \q and his scent has not changed.
en.B: Moab has lived at ease since his youth, resting undisturbed on his dregs, \q never poured out from jar to jar, \q never carried off into exile. \q So his flavor has stayed in him, \q and his aroma is unchanged.
en.R: Moab has lived in peace since the nation began. It is like wine left to sit on its dregs. \q It has never been poured from one jar to another. \q It has never been taken away into exile. \q So it still tastes the same, \q and its smell has not changed.

es.L: Tranquilo ha estado Moab desde su juventud, \q y ha reposado sobre sus heces; \q no ha sido vaciado de vasija en vasija, \q ni ha ido al destierro; \q por eso su sabor ha quedado en él, \q y su aroma no ha cambiado.
es.B: Moab ha vivido tranquilo desde su juventud, reposando sin que nadie lo moviera sobre sus heces, \q nunca trasvasado de tinaja en tinaja, \q nunca llevado al destierro. \q Por eso su sabor se ha conservado, \q y su aroma no ha cambiado.
es.R: Moab ha vivido en paz desde que nació como nación. Es como vino que se deja reposar sobre sus heces. \q Nunca lo han pasado de una tinaja a otra. \q Nunca lo han llevado al destierro. \q Por eso sigue teniendo el mismo sabor, \q y su olor no ha cambiado.

fr.L: Moab a été tranquille dès sa jeunesse, et il a reposé sur sa lie ; \q il n’a pas été vidé de vase en vase, \q et il n’est pas allé en exil ; \q c’est pourquoi son goût est resté en lui, \q et son parfum n’a pas changé.
fr.B: Moab a vécu tranquille depuis sa jeunesse, reposant sans être dérangé sur sa lie, \q jamais transvasé d’une jarre dans une autre, \q jamais emmené en exil. \q Aussi a-t-il gardé sa saveur, \q et son arôme n’a pas changé.
fr.R: Moab a vécu en paix depuis le début de son histoire. Il est comme du vin qu’on a laissé reposer sur sa lie. \q On ne l’a jamais versé d’une jarre dans une autre. \q Il n’a jamais été emmené en exil. \q Alors il a toujours le même goût, \q et son odeur n’a pas changé.

sw.L: Moabu amekuwa na raha tangu ujana wake, naye ametulia juu ya machujo yake; \q hajamiminwa kutoka chombo hadi chombo, \q wala hajakwenda uhamishoni; \q kwa hiyo ladha yake imebaki ndani yake, \q na harufu yake haijabadilika.
sw.B: Moabu ameishi kwa raha tangu ujana wake, akitulia bila kusumbuliwa juu ya machujo yake, \q hajawahi kumiminwa kutoka mtungi hadi mtungi, \q hajawahi kuchukuliwa uhamishoni. \q Kwa hiyo ladha yake imebaki ndani yake, \q na harufu yake haijabadilika.
sw.R: Moabu imeishi kwa amani tangu taifa lilipoanza. Ni kama divai iliyoachwa ikae juu ya machujo yake. \q Haijawahi kumiminwa kutoka mtungi mmoja hadi mwingine. \q Haijawahi kuchukuliwa uhamishoni. \q Kwa hiyo ladha yake bado ni ile ile, \q na harufu yake haijabadilika.

vi.L: Mô-áp đã được an nhàn từ thuở thơ ấu, \q và yên lặng nằm trên cặn rượu của mình; \q nó chưa từng bị rót từ bình này sang bình khác, \q và chưa từng đi lưu đày; \q vì vậy vị của nó vẫn còn trong nó, \q và mùi của nó không thay đổi.
vi.B: Mô-áp sống an nhàn từ thuở thơ ấu, nằm yên trên cặn rượu của mình, \q chưa bao giờ bị rót từ vò này sang vò khác, \q chưa bao giờ bị bắt đi lưu đày. \q Vì thế hương vị nó vẫn còn nguyên, \q và mùi thơm của nó không thay đổi.
vi.R: Từ khi lập quốc, Mô-áp đã sống yên ổn. Nó giống như rượu để yên trên cặn. \q Nó chưa bao giờ bị rót từ vò này sang vò khác. \q Nó chưa bao giờ bị bắt đi lưu đày. \q Vì thế vị của nó vẫn như xưa, \q và mùi của nó chẳng thay đổi.

ko.L: 모압은 어릴 때부터 평안히 지냈고, 자기 찌끼 위에 가라앉아 있었다. \q 이 그릇에서 저 그릇으로 비워진 적이 없고, \q 포로로 끌려간 적도 없다. \q 그래서 그의 맛이 그 안에 그대로 남아 있고, \q 그의 냄새가 변하지 않았다.
ko.B: 모압은 어릴 때부터 평안히 살았고, 찌끼 위에 가라앉은 채 흔들린 적이 없다. \q 이 항아리에서 저 항아리로 옮겨 부어진 적도 없고, \q 포로로 끌려간 적도 없다. \q 그래서 그의 맛이 그대로 남아 있고, \q 그의 향기가 변하지 않았다.
ko.R: 모압은 나라가 생긴 때부터 평안하게 살았다. 모압은 찌끼 위에 그대로 가만히 둔 포도주와 같다. \q 이 항아리에서 저 항아리로 한 번도 옮겨 부어진 적이 없다. \q 한 번도 포로로 끌려간 적이 없다. \q 그래서 그 맛이 그대로이고, \q 그 냄새도 변하지 않았다.

decisions.choice: settled on his dregs, not poured from vessel to vessel: wine left undisturbed
decisions.reason: In winemaking the new wine was left on its lees, the sediment, for a time, then poured off into another jar to clear it. Wine left too long on the dregs grows thick and harsh. Moab is pictured as such wine: never disturbed, never purified by trouble, set in its ways. Zephaniah 1:12 uses the same picture for people "thickening on their dregs", sure that God will do nothing.

decisions.choice: his taste and his scent: Moab's character, unchanged
decisions.reason: The flavor and smell of the wine stand for what Moab is like. Because it has never been "poured out" in exile, its pride and complacency remain (verses 29-30). Verse 12 turns the picture into judgment: now it will be poured out.

decisions.choice: into exile he has not gone: Moab's long security
decisions.reason: Moab had been subdued by Israel's kings (2 Samuel 8:2; 2 Kings 3) and paid tribute to Assyria, but it had not been deported as Israel and Judah were.

decisions.choice: It is like wine left to sit on its dregs
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Moab is pictured as wine, which the Hebrew leaves to the image (m1).

decisions.choice: he, his
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew speaks of Moab as "he", picturing the people as one man; Literal and Balanced keep "he", and Readable says "it".

decisions.choice: sus heces, de vasija en vasija
decisions.reason: Wine left on its dregs grew strong; pouring it from jar to jar cleared it. Moab, never shaken by exile, kept its old character. Moab is masculine in this verse, as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "찌끼 위에 가라앉아", "이 그릇에서 저 그릇으로 비워진 적이 없고"
decisions.reason: The picture of wine left on its lees is kept at every level, with Readable naming the wine, as the English does.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּ֖ה־יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי־ל֥וֹ צֹעִ֖ים וְצֵעֻ֑הוּ וְכֵלָ֣יו יָרִ֔יקוּ וְנִבְלֵיהֶ֖ם יְנַפֵּֽצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will send to him tilters, and they will tilt him, and his vessels they will empty, and their jars they will smash.

en.L: Therefore look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will send to him pourers, and they will pour him out; \q they will empty his vessels \q and smash their jars.
en.B: So the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will send him men who tip out jars, and they will tip him out; \q they will empty his vessels \q and smash their jars to pieces.
en.R: So the time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will send people to pour Moab out like wine. \q They will empty its jars \q and smash them to pieces.

es.L: Por tanto, he aquí vienen días, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que le enviaré trasvasadores que lo trasvasarán; \q vaciarán sus vasijas \q y romperán sus cántaros.
es.B: Por eso vienen días, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que le enviaré hombres que vuelcan tinajas, y lo volcarán; \q vaciarán sus vasijas \q y harán pedazos sus cántaros.
es.R: Por eso se acerca el tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q en que enviaré gente para que derrame a Moab como vino. \q Vaciarán sus tinajas \q y las harán pedazos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, voici, des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où je lui enverrai des transvaseurs, et ils le transvaseront ; \q ils videront ses vases \q et briseront leurs jarres.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où je lui enverrai des gens qui renversent les jarres, et ils le renverseront ; \q ils videront ses vases \q et mettront leurs jarres en pièces.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi un temps vient, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q où j’enverrai des gens pour vider Moab comme du vin. \q Ils videront ses jarres \q et les mettront en pièces.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo tazama, siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapomtumia wamiminaji, nao watammimina; \q watavimwaga vyombo vyake \q na kuivunja mitungi yao.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapomtumia watu wanaomimina mitungi, nao watammimina; \q watavimwaga vyombo vyake \q na kuivunjavunja mitungi yao.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wakati unakuja, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitakapotuma watu waimimine Moabu kama divai. \q Watamwaga mitungi yake \q na kuivunjavunja.

vi.L: Vì vậy, này, những ngày đến, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai đến cùng nó những kẻ rót rượu, và chúng sẽ rót nó ra; \q chúng sẽ làm cạn các bình của nó \q và đập vỡ các vò của chúng.
vi.B: Vì thế những ngày ấy sắp đến, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai đến cùng nó những người nghiêng vò rượu, và họ sẽ đổ nó ra; \q họ sẽ làm cạn các bình của nó \q và đập vỡ tan các vò của chúng.
vi.R: Vì thế sắp đến lúc, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai người đến đổ Mô-áp ra như đổ rượu. \q Họ sẽ làm cạn các vò của nó \q và đập vỡ tan tành.

ko.L: 그러므로 보아라, 날들이 온다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. \q 그때에 내가 그에게 붓는 자들을 보내리니, 그들이 그를 쏟아 버릴 것이다. \q 그들이 그의 그릇들을 비우고, \q 그들의 항아리들을 깨뜨릴 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 때가 오고 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 그때에 내가 그에게 항아리를 기울여 쏟는 자들을 보내리니, 그들이 그를 쏟아 버릴 것이다. \q 그들이 그의 그릇들을 비우고, \q 그 항아리들을 산산이 깨뜨릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그러므로 때가 오고 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 그때에 나는 사람들을 보내어 모압을 포도주처럼 쏟아 버리게 하겠다. \q 그들은 모압의 항아리들을 비우고, \q 그것들을 산산이 깨뜨릴 것이다.

decisions.choice: pourers, who pour him out: the picture of verse 11 turned to judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to tip or tilt a vessel. Moab, the wine that was never poured, will be tipped out by men God sends: the invaders who take its people into exile. Breaking the empty jars means the land itself is wrecked.

decisions.choice: their jars: Moab's people seen as many
decisions.reason: "His vessels" and "their jars" both mean Moab's; the Hebrew moves from Moab as one man to its people as many. The ancient Greek translation reads "his jars" (a claim from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: days are coming: a time God has set
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a coming act of God, in judgment or in rescue (7:32; 30:3).

decisions.choice: men who tip out jars
decisions.reason: Balanced explains the rare word for "pourers". Literal keeps "pourers".

decisions.choice: pour Moab out like wine ... empty its jars and smash them
decisions.reason: Readable says that Moab is pictured as wine and joins the two lines about the vessels and jars into one.

decisions.choice: "Voici, des jours viennent" (L), "Des jours viennent" (B), "Un temps vient" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in French Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "날들이 온다" (L); "때가 오고 있다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for "days are coming" (31:31), one form per level through Jeremiah.

source.text: וּבֹ֥שׁ מוֹאָ֖ב מִכְּמ֑וֹשׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר־בֹּ֨שׁוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ית אֵ֖ל מִבְטֶחָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be ashamed Moab of Chemosh, just as were ashamed [the] house of Israel of Bethel, their confidence.

en.L: And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, \q just as the house of Israel was ashamed \q of Bethel, their confidence.
en.B: Moab will be shamed by Chemosh, \q as the house of Israel was shamed \q by Bethel, the god they relied on.
en.R: Moab will be ashamed of its god Chemosh, \q just as the people of Israel were ashamed \q of Bethel, the place of worship they trusted.

es.L: Y se avergonzará Moab de Quemos, \q como la casa de Israel se avergonzó \q de Betel, su confianza.
es.B: Moab quedará avergonzado por Quemos, \q como la casa de Israel quedó avergonzada \q por Betel, el dios en que confiaba.
es.R: Moab se avergonzará de su dios Quemos, \q así como el pueblo de Israel se avergonzó \q de Betel, el lugar de culto en que confiaba.

fr.L: Et Moab aura honte de Kemosh, \q comme la maison d’Israël a eu honte \q de Béthel, sa confiance.
fr.B: Moab sera déçu par Kemosh \q comme la maison d’Israël a été déçue \q par Béthel, le dieu sur lequel elle comptait.
fr.R: Moab aura honte de son dieu Kemosh, \q comme le peuple d’Israël a eu honte \q de Béthel, le lieu de culte en qui il avait confiance.

sw.L: Na Moabu atamwonea haya Kemoshi, \q kama nyumba ya Israeli ilivyoona haya \q kwa sababu ya Betheli, tumaini lao.
sw.B: Moabu ataaibishwa na Kemoshi, \q kama nyumba ya Israeli ilivyoaibishwa \q na Betheli, mungu waliyemtegemea.
sw.R: Moabu itaona aibu kwa sababu ya mungu wake Kemoshi, \q kama watu wa Israeli walivyoona aibu \q kwa sababu ya Betheli, mahali pa ibada walipopategemea.

vi.L: Mô-áp sẽ hổ thẹn vì Kê-móc, \q như nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên đã hổ thẹn \q vì Bê-tên, là nơi họ tin cậy.
vi.B: Mô-áp sẽ bị Kê-móc làm cho xấu hổ, \q như nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bị xấu hổ \q vì Bê-tên, là thần họ nương cậy.
vi.R: Mô-áp sẽ xấu hổ vì thần Kê-móc của mình, \q như dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã xấu hổ \q vì Bê-tên, là nơi thờ phượng họ đã tin cậy.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 집이 그들이 의지하던 벧엘 때문에 \q 부끄러워했던 것처럼, \q 모압이 그모스 때문에 부끄러워할 것이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 집이 그들이 의지하던 벧엘 때문에 \q 수치를 당했던 것처럼, \q 모압이 그모스 때문에 수치를 당할 것이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성이 그들이 믿었던 예배 장소 벧엘 때문에 \q 부끄러움을 당했던 것처럼, \q 모압은 자기 신 그모스 때문에 부끄러움을 당할 것이다.

decisions.choice: ashamed of: disappointed and disgraced by what one trusted
decisions.reason: To be ashamed of a god is to find that it has failed, and to be shamed for having trusted it (2:36; Isaiah 1:29; 42:17). Chemosh will not save Moab (verse 7).

decisions.choice: Bethel, their confidence: the northern kingdom's shrine, or a god called Bethel
decisions.reason: Jeroboam set up a golden calf at Bethel for the northern kingdom (1 Kings 12:28-29), and Hosea says Israel will be ashamed of that calf (Hosea 10:5-6). When the north fell to Assyria (2 Kings 17), the shrine could not save it. Because Bethel stands beside Chemosh here, some take it as the name of a god, Bethel, known from later records of the region; either way it is the false object of Israel's trust.

decisions.choice: the house of Israel: the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Here "the house of Israel" means the northern tribes, whose shrine was at Bethel and who had already gone into exile (3:6-8).

decisions.choice: the god they relied on
decisions.reason: Balanced takes "their confidence" as the god or shrine they trusted (m2); Literal keeps the bare word.

decisions.choice: its god Chemosh ... the place of worship they trusted
decisions.reason: Readable says that Chemosh is a god and that Bethel was a place of worship (m2).

decisions.choice: The comparison with Israel placed before Moab's shame
decisions.reason: Korean puts the "just as" clause before the main clause; the lines keep the Hebrew's three parts.

source.text: אֵ֚יךְ תֹּֽאמְר֔וּ גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: How can you say, Warriors [are] we, and men of strength for battle?

en.L: How can you say, \q "We [are] warriors, \q and men of valor for battle"?
en.B: How can you claim, \q "We are warriors, \q strong men fit for battle"?
en.R: How can you say, \q "We are strong soldiers. \q We are brave men, ready to fight"?

es.L: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: \q «Valientes [somos], \q y hombres fuertes para la guerra»?
es.B: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} decir: \q «Somos guerreros, \q hombres fuertes preparados para la batalla»?
es.R: ¿Cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} decir: \q «Somos soldados fuertes. \q Somos hombres valientes, listos para pelear»?

fr.L: Comment pouvez-vous dire : \q « Nous [sommes] des guerriers, \q et des hommes vaillants pour le combat » ?
fr.B: Comment osez-vous prétendre : \q « Nous sommes des guerriers, \q des hommes forts, prêts au combat » ?
fr.R: Comment pouvez-vous dire : \q « Nous sommes des soldats forts. \q Nous sommes des hommes courageux, prêts à nous battre » ?

sw.L: Mwawezaje kusema, \q "Sisi [ni] mashujaa, \q na watu hodari kwa vita"?
sw.B: Mwawezaje kujigamba, \q "Sisi ni mashujaa, \q watu wenye nguvu tayari kwa vita"?
sw.R: Mwawezaje kusema, \q "Sisi ni askari wenye nguvu. \q Sisi ni watu hodari, tayari kupigana"?

vi.L: Sao các ngươi nói: \q "Chúng ta [là] dũng sĩ, \q là những người mạnh mẽ để ra trận"?
vi.B: Sao các ngươi dám nói: \q "Chúng ta là chiến binh, \q là những người mạnh mẽ sẵn sàng ra trận"?
vi.R: Sao các ngươi có thể nói: \q "Chúng ta là những người lính mạnh mẽ. \q Chúng ta là những người can đảm, sẵn sàng chiến đấu"?

ko.L: 너희가 어찌 \q "우리는 용사들이요, \q 전쟁에 능한 용맹한 사람들이다" 하고 말하느냐?
ko.B: 너희가 어찌 \q "우리는 용사들이다. \q 싸움에 능한 강한 사람들이다" 하고 말할 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 너희가 어떻게 \q "우리는 강한 군인들이다. \q 우리는 싸울 준비가 된 용감한 사람들이다" 하고 말할 수 있느냐?

decisions.choice: how can you say: a question that rejects the claim
decisions.reason: The question means "You cannot say this" (2:23; 8:8). "You" is plural: the fighting men of Moab, whose boast is quoted.

decisions.choice: men of valor: strong, capable fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean men of strength, ability or wealth; beside "for battle" it means seasoned soldiers.

source.text: שֻׁדַּ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ וְעָרֶ֣יהָ עָלָ֔ה וּמִבְחַ֥ר בַּֽחוּרָ֖יו יָרְד֣וּ לַטָּ֑בַח נְאֻ֨ם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is devastated Moab, and [into] her towns he has gone up, and [the] choice of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name.

en.L: Moab is devastated, and [into] her towns he has gone up, \q and the choicest of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, \q declares the King, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: Moab is ruined, and the enemy has gone up into her towns; \q the finest of her young men have gone down to be slaughtered, \q declares the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: Moab is destroyed, and the enemy has attacked its towns. \q Its best young men have gone down to be killed, \q says the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Devastado está Moab, y [a] sus ciudades subió [el enemigo], \q y lo mejor de sus jóvenes descendió al matadero, \q declara el Rey, \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Moab está en ruinas, y el enemigo ha subido a sus ciudades; \q lo mejor de sus jóvenes ha bajado al matadero, \q afirma el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Moab está destruido, y el enemigo ha atacado sus ciudades. \q Sus mejores jóvenes han caído en la matanza, \q dice el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Moab est dévasté, et [dans] ses villes il est monté, \q et l’élite de ses jeunes gens est descendue au carnage, \q déclare le Roi, \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.B: Moab est ravagé, et l’ennemi est monté dans ses villes ; \q l’élite de ses jeunes gens est descendue à la boucherie, \q déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Moab est détruit, et l’ennemi a attaqué ses villes. \q Ses meilleurs jeunes gens sont descendus pour être tués, \q dit le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Moabu imeharibiwa, na [kwenye] miji yake amepanda, \q na vijana wake bora wameshuka machinjoni, \q asema Mfalme, \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi [ndilo] jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Moabu imeharibiwa, na adui amepanda kuingia katika miji yake; \q vijana wake bora wameshuka kuchinjwa, \q asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Moabu imeangamizwa, na adui ameishambulia miji yake. \q Vijana wake bora wameshuka kuuawa, \q anasema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Mô-áp bị tàn phá, và [kẻ thù] đã lên các thành của nó, \q những thanh niên ưu tú nhất của nó đã đi xuống chỗ bị tàn sát, \q Vua phán vậy, \q danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.B: Mô-áp bị tàn phá, quân thù đã kéo lên các thành của nó; \q những thanh niên giỏi nhất của nó đã đi xuống chỗ bị tàn sát, \q Vua phán vậy, \q là Đấng có danh là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.R: Mô-áp bị hủy diệt, và quân thù đã tấn công các thành của nó. \q Những thanh niên giỏi nhất của nó đã đi xuống chỗ chết, \q Vua phán, \q là Đấng có danh là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.

ko.L: 모압이 황폐해졌고, [원수가] 그의 성읍들에 올라갔으며, \q 그의 가장 뛰어난 젊은이들이 살육을 당하러 내려갔다. \q 왕의 선언이다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.
ko.B: 모압이 망하고, 원수가 그의 성읍들에 쳐들어왔다. \q 그의 가장 뛰어난 젊은이들이 살육을 당하러 내려갔다. \q 왕이 말한다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.
ko.R: 모압은 멸망하고, 원수가 그 성읍들을 공격했다. \q 가장 뛰어난 젊은이들이 죽임을 당하러 내려갔다. \q 왕이 말한다. \q 그 왕의 이름은 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.

decisions.choice: her towns, he has gone up: the enemy has come up into Moab's towns
alternatives: her towns have gone up in smoke
the destroyer of Moab and its towns has come up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and unusual: the verb "has gone up" has no stated subject. Most likely the destroyer of verse 8 has come up against the towns (verse 18 has "the destroyer of Moab has come up"). It may also mean that the towns have gone up in smoke, or, with a small change, "the destroyer of Moab and of its towns has come up".

decisions.choice: the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts: the true king above Moab's king and god
decisions.reason: The title is used again in 46:18 and 51:57. Against Chemosh, who goes into exile (verse 7), and Moab's own king, the LORD is the King who rules the nations.

decisions.choice: gone down to the slaughter: killed like animals led to be slaughtered
decisions.reason: The picture is of a flock going down to the slaughter (11:19; 50:27; 51:40).

decisions.choice: the enemy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject of "has gone up" (m1). Literal keeps "he".

source.text: קָר֥וֹב אֵיד־מוֹאָ֖ב לָב֑וֹא וְרָ֣עָת֔וֹ מִהֲרָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Near [is the] calamity of Moab to come, and his disaster hastens very [much].

en.L: The calamity of Moab is near to come, \q and his disaster hurries very fast.
en.B: Moab's downfall is close at hand; \q its disaster is rushing on.
en.R: Disaster will soon come to Moab. \q It is coming very quickly.

es.L: Cercana está la calamidad de Moab, \q y su desgracia se apresura mucho.
es.B: La ruina de Moab está cerca; \q su desgracia se precipita.
es.R: La desgracia llegará pronto a Moab. \q Viene muy rápido.

fr.L: La ruine de Moab est près d’arriver, \q et son malheur se hâte beaucoup.
fr.B: La chute de Moab est imminente ; \q son malheur arrive à grands pas.
fr.R: Le malheur va bientôt frapper Moab. \q Il arrive très vite.

sw.L: Msiba wa Moabu u karibu kuja, \q na maafa yake yanaharakisha sana.
sw.B: Anguko la Moabu limekaribia; \q maafa yake yanakuja kwa kasi.
sw.R: Maafa yatakuja upesi juu ya Moabu. \q Yanakuja haraka sana.

vi.L: Tai ương của Mô-áp gần đến, \q và họa của nó đến rất nhanh.
vi.B: Ngày sụp đổ của Mô-áp đã gần kề; \q tai họa của nó đang ập đến.
vi.R: Tai họa sắp đến với Mô-áp. \q Nó đang đến rất nhanh.

ko.L: 모압의 재난이 가까이 왔고, \q 그의 재앙이 아주 빨리 다가온다.
ko.B: 모압의 멸망이 가까이 왔고, \q 그의 재앙이 급히 달려온다.
ko.R: 곧 모압에 재앙이 닥칠 것이다. \q 그 재앙이 아주 빨리 오고 있다.

decisions.choice: near is the calamity, it hastens: words from the Song of Moses
decisions.reason: The line echoes Deuteronomy 32:35, "near is the day of their calamity, and what is prepared for them hastens", said of Israel's enemies. The word for calamity is used of the day of a nation's ruin (18:17; 46:21; 49:8).

decisions.choice: its disaster
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "his" for Moab, as the Hebrew has here; Balanced and Readable say "its".

source.text: נֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ כָּל־סְבִיבָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל יֹדְעֵ֣י שְׁמ֑וֹ אִמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֤ה נִשְׁבַּר֙ מַטֵּה־עֹ֔ז מַקֵּ֖ל תִּפְאָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Mourn for him, all [who are] around him, and all knowing his name; say, How is broken [the] staff of strength, [the] rod of splendor!

en.L: Mourn for him, all who are around him, \q and all who know his name; \q say, "How the mighty staff is broken, \q the glorious rod!"
en.B: Grieve for him, all you his neighbors, \q all who know his fame; \q say, "How the mighty scepter is broken, \q the glorious staff!"
en.R: All you nations around Moab, mourn for it. \q All you who know how famous it was, grieve. \q Say, "Moab's mighty power is broken! \q Its glory is gone!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Lamenten|Lamentad}} por él, todos los que están a su alrededor, \q y todos los que conocen su nombre; \q {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: «¡Cómo se ha quebrado la vara fuerte, \q el bastón glorioso!».
es.B: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} duelo por él, todos sus vecinos, \q todos los que conocen su fama; \q {{plural_you:digan|decid}}: «¡Cómo se ha quebrado el cetro poderoso, \q la vara gloriosa!».
es.R: Todas {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, naciones vecinas de Moab, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} por él. \q Todos los que saben lo famoso que era, {{plural_you:lamenten|lamentad}}. \q {{plural_you:Digan|Decid}}: «¡El gran poder de Moab está quebrantado! \q ¡Su gloria se acabó!».

fr.L: Lamentez-vous sur lui, vous tous qui l’entourez, \q et vous tous qui connaissez son nom ; \q dites : « Comme il est brisé, le bâton puissant, \q le sceptre glorieux ! »
fr.B: Pleurez sur lui, vous tous ses voisins, \q vous tous qui connaissez sa renommée ; \q dites : « Comme il est brisé, le sceptre puissant, \q le bâton glorieux ! »
fr.R: Vous, toutes les nations qui entourez Moab, pleurez sur lui. \q Vous tous qui saviez combien il était célèbre, lamentez-vous. \q Dites : « La grande puissance de Moab est brisée ! \q Sa gloire a disparu ! »

sw.L: Mwombolezeni, ninyi nyote mlio kando yake, \q na wote mnaolijua jina lake; \q semeni, "Jinsi gongo la nguvu lilivyovunjika, \q fimbo ya fahari!"
sw.B: Mwombolezeni, enyi jirani zake wote, \q nyote mnaoijua sifa yake; \q semeni, "Jinsi fimbo ya enzi yenye nguvu ilivyovunjika, \q fimbo tukufu!"
sw.R: Enyi mataifa yote mliozunguka Moabu, ilieni. \q Enyi nyote mnaojua jinsi ilivyokuwa maarufu, huzunikeni. \q Semeni, "Nguvu kuu ya Moabu imevunjika! \q Utukufu wake umetoweka!"

vi.L: Hỡi mọi kẻ ở chung quanh nó, \q và mọi kẻ biết danh nó, hãy than khóc nó; \q hãy nói: "Cây gậy quyền năng, \q cây trượng vinh hiển đã gãy thể nào!"
vi.B: Hỡi mọi lân bang của nó, \q mọi kẻ biết danh tiếng nó, hãy khóc thương nó; \q hãy nói: "Cây quyền trượng uy nghi đã gãy thể nào, \q cây gậy vinh hiển kia!"
vi.R: Hỡi mọi dân tộc chung quanh Mô-áp, hãy than khóc nó. \q Hỡi mọi người biết danh tiếng nó, hãy buồn thương. \q Hãy nói: "Quyền lực lớn lao của Mô-áp đã bị bẻ gãy! \q Vinh quang của nó đã mất rồi!"

ko.L: 그의 주위에 있는 모든 자들아, 그를 위하여 애도하여라. \q 그의 이름을 아는 모든 자들아, \q 말하여라. "어찌하여 힘센 지팡이가, \q 영광스러운 막대기가 부러졌는가!"
ko.B: 그의 이웃들아, 그를 위하여 슬퍼하여라. \q 그의 명성을 아는 모든 자들아, \q 이렇게 말하여라. "어찌하여 강한 홀이, \q 영광스러운 지팡이가 부러졌는가!"
ko.R: 모압 주위에 있는 모든 나라들아, 모압을 위하여 슬퍼하여라. \q 모압이 얼마나 이름났는지 아는 모든 사람들아, 슬퍼하여라. \q 이렇게 말하여라. "모압의 강한 힘이 꺾였다! \q 모압의 영광이 사라졌다!"

decisions.choice: mourn: shake the head in sorrow
decisions.reason: The verb means to sway or shake the head, a gesture of grief and sympathy with those who suffer (15:5; 16:5; 22:10; Job 2:11).

decisions.choice: all who know his name: all who know of Moab's fame
decisions.reason: "Name" here is reputation. Those near and far are called to lament.

decisions.choice: the mighty staff, the glorious rod: the power of Moab's rule
decisions.reason: The staff is the rod a ruler holds, and so stands for kingly power (Psalm 110:2; Ezekiel 19:11-14). The two lines say the same thing twice: Moab's might and splendor are broken. "How" opens a lament, as in Lamentations 1:1.

decisions.choice: scepter
decisions.reason: Balanced says "scepter" for the first word, which means a royal staff here (m3), and "staff" for the second; Literal keeps "staff" and "rod".

decisions.choice: All you nations around Moab ... Moab's mighty power is broken
decisions.reason: Readable names who is called to mourn and says what the staff stands for (m3).

decisions.choice: "힘센 지팡이 ... 영광스러운 막대기" (L); "강한 홀 ... 영광스러운 지팡이" (B); "강한 힘 ... 영광" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of the ruler's staff; Readable says what it stands for, as the English Readable does.

source.text: רְדִ֤י מִכָּבוֹד֙ וּשְׁבִ֣י בַצָּמָ֔א יֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־דִּיב֑וֹן כִּֽי־שֹׁדֵ֤ד מוֹאָב֙ עָ֣לָה בָ֔ךְ שִׁחֵ֖ת מִבְצָרָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Come down from glory, and sit in thirst, inhabitant, daughter of Dibon, for [the] destroyer of Moab has come up against you, he has ruined your strongholds.

en.L: Come down from glory and sit in thirst, \q inhabitant, daughter of Dibon; \q for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you, \q he has ruined your strongholds.
en.B: Come down from your glory and sit on the parched ground, \q you who live in Daughter Dibon, \q for Moab's destroyer has come up against you; \q he has torn down your fortresses.
en.R: People of Dibon, come down from your place of honor. \q Sit on the dry ground. \q The enemy who destroys Moab has come to attack you. \q He has torn down your strong walls.

es.L: Desciende de la gloria y siéntate en tierra seca, \q moradora, hija de Dibón; \q porque el destructor de Moab ha subido contra ti, \q ha arruinado tus fortalezas.
es.B: Baja de tu gloria y siéntate en el suelo reseco, \q tú que habitas en la hija de Dibón, \q porque el destructor de Moab ha subido contra ti; \q ha derribado tus fortalezas.
es.R: Pueblo de Dibón, baja de tu lugar de honor. \q Siéntate en el suelo seco. \q El enemigo que destruye a Moab ha venido a atacarte. \q Ha derribado tus murallas fuertes.

fr.L: Descends de la gloire et assieds-toi dans la soif, \q habitante, fille de Dibon ; \q car le dévastateur de Moab est monté contre toi, \q il a ruiné tes forteresses.
fr.B: Descends de ta gloire et assieds-toi sur la terre desséchée, \q toi qui habites la fille de Dibon, \q car le dévastateur de Moab est monté contre toi ; \q il a démoli tes forteresses.
fr.R: Habitants de Dibon, descendez de votre place d’honneur. \q Asseyez-vous sur le sol sec. \q L’ennemi qui détruit Moab est venu vous attaquer. \q Il a démoli vos murailles.

sw.L: Shuka kutoka katika utukufu, ukae katika kiu, \q ewe mkaaji, binti Diboni; \q kwa maana mharibu wa Moabu amepanda juu yako, \q ameziharibu ngome zako.
sw.B: Shuka kutoka katika utukufu wako, ukae juu ya ardhi kavu, \q wewe ukaaye Binti Diboni, \q kwa maana mharibu wa Moabu amepanda juu yako; \q amezibomoa ngome zako.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Diboni, shukeni kutoka mahali penu pa heshima. \q Kaeni juu ya ardhi kavu. \q Adui mwangamizi wa Moabu amekuja kuwashambulia. \q Amebomoa kuta zenu imara.

vi.L: Hãy từ nơi vinh hiển xuống, ngồi trong cảnh khát, \q hỡi kẻ cư ngụ, con gái Đi-bôn; \q vì kẻ tàn phá Mô-áp đã lên đánh ngươi, \q nó đã phá hủy các đồn lũy ngươi.
vi.B: Hãy rời nơi vinh hiển mà ngồi trên đất khô cằn, \q hỡi dân cư của con gái Đi-bôn, \q vì kẻ tàn phá Mô-áp đã kéo lên đánh ngươi; \q nó đã phá đổ các đồn lũy ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Đi-bôn, hãy rời chỗ danh dự của mình. \q Hãy ngồi trên đất khô. \q Quân thù hủy diệt Mô-áp đã đến tấn công ngươi. \q Nó đã phá đổ các tường thành kiên cố của ngươi.

ko.L: 딸 디본에 사는 자야, \q 영광에서 내려와 목마른 채 앉아라. \q 모압을 멸망시키는 자가 너를 치러 올라와서 \q 네 요새들을 무너뜨렸다.
ko.B: 딸 디본에 사는 자야, \q 영광의 자리에서 내려와 메마른 땅에 앉아라. \q 모압을 멸망시키는 자가 너를 치러 올라와서 \q 네 요새들을 허물었다.
ko.R: 디본 백성아, 영광스러운 자리에서 내려오너라. \q 메마른 땅에 앉아라. \q 모압을 멸망시키는 원수가 너를 치러 왔다. \q 그가 너의 튼튼한 성벽들을 허물었다.

decisions.choice: daughter of Dibon: the city and its people pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: As with "daughter of Zion", the city is spoken of as a woman. Dibon, north of the Arnon (Numbers 21:30; Isaiah 15:2), was a chief city of Moab; the inscription of Mesha king of Moab was found there.

decisions.choice: come down from glory, sit in thirst: from honor to humiliation
alternatives: sit in filth (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The city, once seated in honor, must come down and sit on the thirsty ground, as captives and mourners sat in the dust (Isaiah 47:1). "Sit" plays on "inhabitant", which is from the same verb: she who sits enthroned must sit in the dust. The written text has a slightly different form of "sit"; the reading tradition gives the command.

decisions.choice: the destroyer ... has ruined your strongholds
decisions.reason: The destroyer is the invader of verse 8. The verbs are in the completed form, as in a vision of what is certain.

decisions.choice: you who live in Daughter Dibon
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the wording "Daughter Zion" settled in Isaiah for such titles.

decisions.choice: People of Dibon ... your place of honor
decisions.reason: Readable explains "daughter of Dibon" as the city's people and "glory" as their place of honor.

source.text: אֶל־דֶּ֛רֶךְ עִמְדִ֥י וְצַפִּ֖י יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת עֲרוֹעֵ֑ר שַׁאֲלִי־נָ֣ס וְנִמְלָ֔טָה אִמְרִ֖י מַה־נִּֽהְיָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: By [the] road stand and watch, inhabitant of Aroer; ask [the] fleeing [man] and [the] escaping [woman]; say, What has happened?

en.L: Stand by the road and watch, inhabitant of Aroer; \q ask the man who flees and the woman who escapes; \q say, "What has happened?"
en.B: Stand by the road and keep watch, you who live in Aroer! \q Ask the man who is running and the woman who is escaping; \q ask them, "What has happened?"
en.R: People of Aroer, stand beside the road and watch. \q Ask the men and women who are running away, \q "What has happened?"

es.L: Ponte junto al camino y vigila, moradora de Aroer; \q pregunta al que huye y a la que escapa; \q di: «¿Qué ha sucedido?».
es.B: ¡Ponte junto al camino y vigila, tú que habitas en Aroer! \q Pregúntale al hombre que corre y a la mujer que escapa; \q pregúntales: «¿Qué ha pasado?».
es.R: Gente de Aroer, {{plural_you:párense|paraos}} junto al camino y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}. \q {{plural_you:Pregúntenles|Preguntadles}} a los hombres y a las mujeres que huyen: \q «¿Qué ha pasado?».

fr.L: Tiens-toi sur le chemin et guette, habitante d’Aroër ; \q interroge celui qui fuit et celle qui s’échappe ; \q dis : « Qu’est-il arrivé ? »
fr.B: Tiens-toi au bord du chemin et fais le guet, toi qui habites Aroër ! \q Interroge l’homme qui s’enfuit et la femme qui s’échappe ; \q demande-leur : « Que s’est-il passé ? »
fr.R: Habitants d’Aroër, tenez-vous au bord de la route et regardez. \q Demandez aux hommes et aux femmes qui s’enfuient : \q « Que s’est-il passé ? »

sw.L: Simama kando ya njia, uangalie, ewe mkaaji wa Aroeri; \q mwulize mwanamume anayekimbia na mwanamke anayeokoka; \q sema, "Ni nini kilichotokea?"
sw.B: Simama kando ya njia, ukeshe, wewe ukaaye Aroeri! \q Mwulize mwanamume anayekimbia na mwanamke anayetoroka; \q waulize, "Kumetokea nini?"
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Aroeri, simameni kando ya barabara, mtazame. \q Waulizeni wanaume na wanawake wanaokimbia, \q "Kumetokea nini?"

vi.L: Hãy đứng bên đường mà trông, hỡi dân cư A-rô-e; \q hãy hỏi người đàn ông chạy trốn và người đàn bà thoát nạn; \q hãy hỏi: "Đã xảy ra chuyện gì?"
vi.B: Hỡi dân cư A-rô-e, hãy đứng bên đường mà canh chừng! \q Hãy hỏi người đàn ông đang chạy trốn và người đàn bà đang thoát thân; \q hãy hỏi họ: "Đã xảy ra chuyện gì?"
vi.R: Hỡi dân A-rô-e, hãy đứng bên đường mà nhìn. \q Hãy hỏi những người đàn ông và đàn bà đang chạy trốn: \q "Đã xảy ra chuyện gì vậy?"

ko.L: 아로엘에 사는 자야, 길가에 서서 지켜보아라. \q 도망하는 남자와 피하는 여자에게 물어라. \q 말하여라. "무슨 일이 일어났느냐?"
ko.B: 아로엘에 사는 자야, 길가에 서서 살펴보아라! \q 달아나는 남자와 피하는 여자에게 \q "무슨 일이 일어났느냐?" 하고 물어보아라.
ko.R: 아로엘 백성아, 길가에 서서 지켜보아라. \q 도망치는 남자들과 여자들에게 \q "무슨 일이 일어났소?" 하고 물어보아라.

decisions.choice: Aroer: a town on the rim of the Arnon gorge
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the north edge of the Arnon valley, on the main road (Deuteronomy 2:36; Joshua 13:9, 16). From there the people would see the refugees coming from the north.

decisions.choice: the man who flees and the woman who escapes: everyone in flight
decisions.reason: One verb is masculine and the other feminine, so the pair means all the refugees, men and women alike. The answer to the question comes in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the men and women who are running away
decisions.reason: Readable joins the pair into one phrase (m2).

source.text: הֹבִ֥ישׁ מוֹאָ֛ב כִּֽי־חַ֖תָּה הֵילִ֣ילוּ׀וּֽזְעָ֑קוּ הַגִּ֣ידוּ בְאַרְנ֔וֹן כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Is put to shame Moab, for it is shattered; wail and cry out! Tell in [the] Arnon that is devastated Moab.

en.L: Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered; wail and cry out! \q Tell [it] by the Arnon \q that Moab is devastated.
en.B: Moab is disgraced, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! \q Announce it by the Arnon: \q Moab is ruined!
en.R: Moab is put to shame and broken. Cry and wail! \q Tell the news beside the Arnon River: \q Moab is destroyed!

es.L: Avergonzado está Moab, porque está quebrantado; ¡{{plural_you:giman|gemid}} y {{plural_you:clamen|clamad}}! \q {{plural_you:Anuncien|Anunciad}} en el Arnón \q que Moab está devastado.
es.B: Moab está humillado, porque está destrozado. ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}} y {{plural_you:griten|gritad}}! \q {{plural_you:Anúncienlo|Anunciadlo}} junto al Arnón: \q ¡Moab está en ruinas!
es.R: Moab está avergonzado y destrozado. ¡{{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} y {{plural_you:griten|gritad}}! \q {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} la noticia junto al río Arnón: \q ¡Moab está destruido!

fr.L: Moab est couvert de honte, car il est brisé ; lamentez-vous et criez ! \q Annoncez[-le] au bord de l’Arnon : \q Moab est dévasté.
fr.B: Moab est déshonoré, car il est brisé. Lamentez-vous et criez ! \q Annoncez-le au bord de l’Arnon : \q Moab est ravagé !
fr.R: Moab est couvert de honte et brisé. Pleurez et lamentez-vous ! \q Annoncez la nouvelle au bord de la rivière Arnon : \q Moab est détruit !

sw.L: Moabu imeaibishwa, kwa maana imevunjwa; pigeni yowe na kulia! \q Tangazeni [habari] kando ya Arnoni \q kwamba Moabu imeharibiwa.
sw.B: Moabu imeaibishwa, kwa maana imevunjwavunjwa. Pigeni yowe na kulia! \q Tangazeni kando ya Arnoni: \q Moabu imeangamia!
sw.R: Moabu imeaibishwa na kuvunjwa. Lieni na kupiga yowe! \q Pelekeni habari kando ya Mto Arnoni: \q Moabu imeangamizwa!

vi.L: Mô-áp bị hổ thẹn, vì nó bị đập tan; hãy than van và kêu la! \q Hãy báo tin bên sông Ạt-nôn \q rằng Mô-áp đã bị tàn phá.
vi.B: Mô-áp bị sỉ nhục, vì nó đã bị đập tan. Hãy than van và kêu la! \q Hãy loan báo bên sông Ạt-nôn: \q Mô-áp đã điêu tàn!
vi.R: Mô-áp bị sỉ nhục và bị đập tan. Hãy khóc lóc và than van! \q Hãy báo tin bên bờ sông Ạt-nôn: \q Mô-áp đã bị hủy diệt!

ko.L: 모압이 수치를 당했다. 그것이 부서졌다. 울부짖고 부르짖어라! \q 아르논 가에 알려라. \q 모압이 황폐해졌다고.
ko.B: 모압이 치욕을 당했다. 산산이 부서졌다. 울부짖고 부르짖어라! \q 아르논 강가에 알려라. \q 모압이 망했다!
ko.R: 모압은 수치를 당하고 부서졌다. 울며 부르짖어라! \q 아르논 강가에 소식을 전하여라. \q 모압이 멸망했다!

decisions.choice: Moab is put to shame ... wail: the refugees' answer, then a call to mourn
decisions.reason: The first words answer the question of verse 19. The commands to wail and cry out are plural in the reading tradition; the written text has them singular, addressed to the woman of Aroer. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the Arnon: the river gorge at the heart of Moab
decisions.reason: The Arnon runs west through a deep canyon into the Dead Sea (Numbers 21:13; Isaiah 16:2). News told there would spread through the whole land.

decisions.choice: the Arnon River
decisions.reason: Readable says that the Arnon is a river.

source.text: וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל־חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל־יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל־מֵיפָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And judgment has come to [the] land of the plateau, to Holon and to Jahaz and upon Mephaath,

en.L: And judgment has come to the land of the plateau, to Holon and to Jahaz and upon Mephaath,

decisions.choice: verses 21-24: a list of the towns judged, set as prose
decisions.reason: The poem pauses for a list of towns on the plateau, all governed by "judgment has come". The accents give the list no parallel lines (verses 22 and 23 are each a single unit), so verses 21-24 are set as prose. The towns are named in no geographical order and end with "all the towns of the land of Moab" (verse 24).

decisions.choice: Holon, Jahaz, Mephaath: towns of the plateau
decisions.reason: Jahaz is where Israel defeated Sihon (Numbers 21:23); here the name has an ending meaning "to", as in Numbers 21:23. Mephaath was given to Reuben and became a Levite town (Joshua 13:18; 21:37); the written text spells it slightly differently. This Holon is known only here, not the town of Judah (Joshua 15:51).

decisions.choice: judgment: God's sentence carried out
decisions.reason: The word is used for a verdict and its execution. It returns in verse 47, "thus far the judgment of Moab".

decisions.choice: Jahaz
decisions.reason: The town keeps the form "Jahaz" used in verse 34, Isaiah 15:4 and Numbers 21:23.

decisions.choice: Jahaza
decisions.reason: The town Jahaz, in the form published at Joshua 13:18, where the Hebrew also ends in -ah (Jahaza); verse 34 has Jahaz; the towns of verses 21-24 follow the published forms where they exist.

decisions.choice: Gia-hác, Mê-phát and the other towns of Moab
decisions.reason: The towns of verses 21-24 are written as Joshua 13 and 21 and 1 Chronicles 6 have them where they are published; the rest are new, in the same pattern.

decisions.choice: The town names in verses 21-24 in the Protestant spellings (홀론, 야하스, 메바앗, 디본, 느보, 벧디블라다임, 기랴다임, 벧가물, 벧므온, 그리옷, 보스라)
decisions.reason: As published for the same towns in Numbers and Joshua where they occur; the list is prose, as the English sets it.

decisions.choice: horn and arm: strength and power
decisions.reason: A horn is the strength of a wild ox or ram, and so of a people or king (1 Samuel 2:1; Psalm 75:11; Lamentations 2:3). The arm is power to act and fight (Psalm 10:15; Ezekiel 30:21). Both are broken: Moab can no longer defend itself.

decisions.reason: Readable keeps the pictures and says what they mean (m1).

sw.L: Mlevyeni, \q kwa maana amejitukuza juu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q naye Moabu atagaagaa katika matapishi yake, \q naye pia atakuwa kitu cha kuchekwa.

decisions.choice: make him drunk: the cup of God's anger
decisions.reason: The command takes up the cup of wrath that the nations must drink in 25:15-29, where Moab is named (25:21), and they "drink and get drunk and vomit" (25:27). Drunkenness pictures helpless ruin and disgrace (13:13; 51:39).

decisions.choice: against the LORD he has made himself great: Moab's pride is defiance of God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself great, to boast or act arrogantly against God (Psalm 35:26; Zephaniah 2:8, 10, said of Moab and Ammon). The reason is repeated in verse 42.

decisions.choice: wallow: splash or flounder
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to clap or strike the hands; here it pictures the drunkard falling and floundering in his own vomit.

decisions.choice: he too: Moab, who mocked others, will be mocked
decisions.reason: "He too" points ahead to verse 27: Moab laughed at Israel, and now Moab will be laughed at.

decisions.choice: something to laugh at
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for "laughingstock"; Literal keeps the word.

records.literal_gloss: And was not the laughingstock to you Israel? Or among thieves was he found, that as often as your words about him you shook yourself?

en.L: And was not Israel the laughingstock to you? \q Or was he found among thieves, \q that whenever you spoke of him you shook your head?
en.B: Was not Israel a joke to you? \q Was he caught among thieves, \q that every time you spoke of him you shook your head in scorn?
en.R: Moab, did you not laugh at Israel? \q Was Israel caught with thieves? \q Every time you talked about Israel, you shook your head to mock it.

es.L: ¿Y no fue Israel objeto de burla para ti? \q ¿Acaso fue sorprendido entre ladrones, \q para que cada vez que hablabas de él movieras la cabeza?
es.B: ¿No fue Israel motivo de burla para ti? \q ¿Lo atraparon entre ladrones, \q para que cada vez que hablabas de él movieras la cabeza con desprecio?
es.R: Moab, ¿no te reíste de Israel? \q ¿Acaso atraparon a Israel con ladrones? \q Cada vez que hablabas de Israel, movías la cabeza para burlarte.

fr.L: Et Israël n’a-t-il pas été pour toi un objet de risée ? \q Ou bien a-t-il été trouvé parmi des voleurs, \q pour que, chaque fois que tu parlais de lui, tu hoches la tête ?
fr.B: Israël n’était-il pas pour toi un sujet de moquerie ? \q L’avait-on surpris parmi des voleurs, \q pour que chaque fois que tu parlais de lui, tu hoches la tête avec mépris ?
fr.R: Moab, ne t’es-tu pas moqué d’Israël ? \q Israël avait-il été pris avec des voleurs ? \q Chaque fois que tu parlais d’Israël, tu hochais la tête pour te moquer de lui.

sw.L: Je, Israeli hakuwa kitu cha kuchekwa kwako? \q Au je, alionekana kati ya wezi, \q hata kila ulipomtaja ukatikisa kichwa?
sw.B: Je, Israeli hakuwa kitu cha mzaha kwako? \q Je, alikamatwa pamoja na wezi, \q hata kila ulipomtaja ukatikisa kichwa kwa dharau?
sw.R: Ewe Moabu, je, hukuwacheka Israeli? \q Je, Israeli walikamatwa pamoja na wezi? \q Kila ulipozungumza juu ya Israeli, ulitikisa kichwa kuwadhihaki.

vi.L: Chẳng phải Y-sơ-ra-ên đã là trò cười cho ngươi sao? \q Hay nó bị bắt gặp giữa bọn trộm cướp, \q mà hễ khi nói đến nó là ngươi lắc đầu?
vi.B: Chẳng phải ngươi đã xem Y-sơ-ra-ên là trò cười sao? \q Nó có bị bắt quả tang giữa bọn trộm đâu, \q mà mỗi khi nói về nó ngươi lại lắc đầu khinh bỉ?
vi.R: Hỡi Mô-áp, chẳng phải ngươi đã cười nhạo Y-sơ-ra-ên sao? \q Y-sơ-ra-ên có bị bắt quả tang với bọn trộm đâu? \q Thế mà mỗi lần nói về Y-sơ-ra-ên, ngươi lại lắc đầu chế nhạo.

ko.L: 이스라엘이 너에게 웃음거리가 아니었느냐? \q 그가 도둑들 가운데서 붙잡혔느냐? \q 네가 그에 관하여 말할 때마다 머리를 흔들었으니.
ko.B: 이스라엘이 너에게 조롱거리가 아니었느냐? \q 그가 도둑들과 함께 붙잡히기라도 했느냐? \q 네가 그 이야기를 할 때마다 비웃으며 머리를 흔들었으니.
ko.R: 모압아, 너는 이스라엘을 비웃지 않았느냐? \q 이스라엘이 도둑들과 함께 붙잡히기라도 했느냐? \q 너는 이스라엘 이야기를 할 때마다 머리를 흔들며 조롱했다.

decisions.choice: was not Israel ...? Or was he found ...?: questions that accuse Moab
decisions.reason: "You" is Moab. The first question means that Moab did mock Israel; the second asks whether Israel had done anything to deserve it, as if caught red-handed among thieves (2:26). The answer expected is no. Moab's scorn for Israel is condemned also in Zephaniah 2:8 and Ezekiel 25:8.

decisions.choice: you shook yourself: you shook your head in mockery
decisions.reason: Shaking or wagging the head was a gesture of scorn (18:16; Psalm 44:15; Lamentations 2:15). The verb is from the same root as "mourn" in verse 17, but here it is mockery.

decisions.choice: was he found: the reading of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The reading tradition has the masculine "he was found", for Israel; the written text has the feminine form. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Moab, ...
decisions.reason: Readable names the one addressed (m1).

source.text: עִזְב֤וּ עָרִים֙ וְשִׁכְנ֣וּ בַּסֶּ֔לַע יֹשְׁבֵ֖י מוֹאָ֑ב וִֽהְי֣וּ כְיוֹנָ֔ה תְּקַנֵּ֖ן בְּעֶבְרֵ֥י פִי־פָֽחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: Leave [the] towns and dwell in the rock, inhabitants of Moab, and be like a dove [that] nests in [the] sides of [the] mouth of [the] chasm.

en.L: Leave the towns and dwell in the rock, \q inhabitants of Moab; \q and be like a dove that nests \q in the sides of the mouth of a chasm.
en.B: Abandon the towns and live among the rocks, \q you people of Moab! \q Be like a dove that makes its nest \q in the cliffs beside the mouth of a gorge.
en.R: People of Moab, leave your towns. \q Go and live among the rocks. \q Be like a dove that builds its nest \q high on the sides of a deep canyon.

es.L: {{plural_you:Abandonen|Abandonad}} las ciudades y {{plural_you:habiten|habitad}} en la peña, \q moradores de Moab; \q y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} como la paloma que anida \q en los bordes de la boca de la sima.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Abandonen|Abandonad}} las ciudades y {{plural_you:vivan|vivid}} entre las rocas, \q habitantes de Moab! \q {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como la paloma que hace su nido \q en los peñascos a la entrada de un barranco.
es.R: Gente de Moab, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}}. \q {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a vivir entre las rocas. \q {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como la paloma que hace su nido \q en lo alto de las paredes de un cañón profundo.

fr.L: Quittez les villes et habitez dans le rocher, \q habitants de Moab ; \q et soyez comme une colombe qui fait son nid \q sur les flancs de l’entrée d’un gouffre.
fr.B: Abandonnez les villes et vivez parmi les rochers, \q habitants de Moab ! \q Soyez comme une colombe qui fait son nid \q dans les parois, à l’entrée d’une gorge.
fr.R: Habitants de Moab, quittez vos villes. \q Allez vivre parmi les rochers. \q Soyez comme une colombe qui fait son nid \q tout en haut des parois d’un profond ravin.

sw.L: Iacheni miji, mkakae mwambani, \q enyi wakaaji wa Moabu; \q mkawe kama njiwa awekaye kiota \q pembeni mwa kinywa cha bonde refu.
sw.B: Iacheni miji mkakae kati ya miamba, \q enyi watu wa Moabu! \q Muwe kama njiwa anayejenga kiota chake \q katika miamba iliyo kando ya mlango wa korongo.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Moabu, ondokeni mijini mwenu. \q Nendeni mkakae kati ya miamba. \q Muwe kama njiwa anayejenga kiota chake \q juu kwenye kingo za korongo refu.

vi.L: Hãy bỏ các thành mà ở trong vầng đá, \q hỡi dân cư Mô-áp; \q hãy như chim bồ câu làm tổ \q ở hai bên miệng vực sâu.
vi.B: Hãy bỏ các thành mà sống giữa núi đá, \q hỡi dân Mô-áp! \q Hãy như chim bồ câu làm tổ \q trên vách đá bên miệng hẻm núi.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Mô-áp, hãy rời bỏ các thành. \q Hãy đi sống giữa núi đá. \q Hãy như chim bồ câu làm tổ \q cao trên vách của một hẻm núi sâu.

ko.L: 모압에 사는 자들아, \q 성읍들을 떠나 바위틈에서 살아라. \q 깊은 골짜기 어귀 양쪽에 \q 둥지를 트는 비둘기처럼 되어라.
ko.B: 모압 백성아, \q 성읍들을 버리고 바위 사이에서 살아라! \q 골짜기 어귀 낭떠러지에 \q 둥지를 트는 비둘기처럼 되어라.
ko.R: 모압 백성아, 너희 성읍들을 떠나라. \q 바위 사이에 가서 살아라. \q 깊은 골짜기 높은 절벽에 \q 둥지를 트는 비둘기처럼 되어라.

decisions.choice: like a dove nesting in the cliffs: hiding where the enemy cannot reach
